# SRX Global Announces Activation of the University of California, Davis as a Clinical Trial Site for CERo Therapeutics’ Ongoing Phase 1 CERTAIN-T Trial of CER-1236 in Hematologic Malignancies


October 26, 2026 9:05am EDT


*UC Davis is the primary manufacturing site for CER-1236, site activation is expected to expand patient recruitment capacity and streamline treatment logistics*


*Update follows SRX’s previously announced definitive agreement to acquire CERo Therapeutics*


NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the “Company” or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies and strategic assets, today announced that the University of California, Davis (“UC Davis”) has been activated as a clinical trial site for CERTAIN-T, the ongoing Phase 1 study evaluating CER-1236 in patients with hematologic malignancies being conducted by CERo Therapeutics, the operating subsidiary of CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. (OTCQB: CERO) (“CERo Holdings” and, together with CERo Therapeutics, “CERo”), an innovative cellular immunotherapy company advancing engineered T cell therapeutics designed to engage phagocytic mechanisms. UC Davis also serves as the primary manufacturing site for CER-1236.


The activation of UC Davis is expected to expand patient recruitment capacity while leveraging the site's existing manufacturing capabilities to streamline treatment logistics.


“Activating UC Davis as a clinical site is a meaningful operational milestone for CERo and for the CERTAIN-T study,” said Kent Cunningham, Chief Executive Officer of SRX Global. “Bringing manufacturing and patient enrollment together at a single, highly regarded academic institution, streamlines logistics while strengthening the overall clinical trial footprint. This progress reinforces our conviction in CERo’s differentiated approach to engineered T cell therapeutics, and we look forward to continuing to support the team as we work toward closing the proposed acquisition.”


Brian Jonas, M.D., Professor, clinician-scientist, and Chief of the Division of Malignant Hematology, Cellular Therapy and Transplantation in the Department of Internal Medicine at the UC Davis School of Medicine and UC Davis Comprehensive Cancer Center and study investigator on the trial, commented, “We are excited to join with CERo Therapeutics to open this important clinical trial site. We look forward to being able to offer a novel and innovative chimeric engulfment receptor-based treatment option for our patients with myeloid malignancies.”


Chris Ehrlich, CERo Therapeutics CEO added, "The addition of UC Davis represents another important milestone in our collaboration, expanding our longstanding relationship beyond manufacturing to include patient enrollment in the CERTAIN-T study. Integrating manufacturing and clinical operations at a single institution has the potential to expand patient access while shortening the time between cell manufacturing and patient infusion. We have been encouraged by the interest we've received from investigators and institutions evaluating participation in the CERTAIN-T trial, and we are pleased to welcome the UC Davis team."


CERo previously reported findings from six patients treated in the first two cohorts of CERTAIN-T. All three patients in the second cohort completed the 28-day dose-limiting toxicity (“DLT”) assessment without a DLT. In its June 2026 update, CERo reported that the observed safety profile remained consistent with earlier findings of no cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, DLTs or treatment-related severe adverse events during the DLT assessment window. Investigators reported clinical improvement in two patients, although formal response assessments remained ongoing. One patient with refractory acute myeloid leukemia (“AML”) subsequently underwent allogeneic stem cell transplantation 71 days after CER-1236 infusion. The study has expanded to include myelodysplastic syndromes (“MDS”) and myelofibrosis (“MF”). These clinical results are preliminary and are not sufficient to establish the safety or efficacy of CER-1236.


On October 7, 2026, SRX announced that it had entered into a definitive purchase agreement under which CERo Therapeutics will become a wholly owned subsidiary of SRX Global. The proposed transaction followed SRX’s purchase of senior secured debt in CERo Holdings, announced on August 31, 2026, and remains subject to customary closing conditions.


**About the CERTAIN-T Trial**
The first-in-human, multicenter, open-label Phase 1/1b CERTAIN-T study is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary clinical activity of CER-1236 in patients with hematologic malignancies. The study initially enrolled patients with acute myeloid leukemia (“AML”), including relapsed/refractory AML, AML with measurable residual disease (MRD), and newly diagnosed TP53-mutated AML, and has since expanded to include transfusion-dependent myelodysplastic syndromes (“TD-MDS”), high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (“HR-MDS”), and post-JAK inhibitor myelofibrosis (“MF”). Primary endpoints include safety and tolerability. Secondary endpoints include pharmacokinetics and measures of clinical response, including overall response rate (“ORR”), complete response (“CR”), composite complete response (“cCR”), and measurable residual disease (“MRD”).


**About SRX Global Inc.**
SRX Global is an AI-driven platform focused on generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies, strategic assets, and technology-enabled opportunities. The Company leverages proprietary technology, data analytics, and disciplined capital allocation to identify and manage investments across multiple sectors.


**About CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc.**
CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. is an innovative immunotherapy company advancing the development of engineered T cell therapeutics for the treatment of cancer. The Company’s proprietary approach to T cell engineering is designed to integrate characteristics of innate and adaptive immunity into a single therapeutic construct intended to engage multiple immune mechanisms against cancer. CERo refers to these engineered cells as Chimeric Engulfment Receptor T cells (“CER-T”).


The Company’s lead investigational product candidate, CER-1236, is being evaluated in hematologic malignancies.
